- label: just the type name, e.g. "Refrigerator", "Washer" (title case, 1-2 words).
- desc: 30-45 words of REAL, brand-relevant detail about {brand} repair specifically FOR THAT TAB'S OWN TYPE — what tends to go wrong on this brand's models of that type, what the local provider {business} connects you with actually checks or fixes. Do not repeat the same sentence structure across tabs, and do not blur two types together in one tab. Plain text only, no HTML tags.

Choose brand-typical detail. Do NOT invent specific model numbers, exact error codes, or statistics.

ACCURACY RULES (critical): Use only well-established general knowledge about {city}'s region, climate, and seasons. Do NOT invent or state as fact: statistics, prices, pass/success rates, review counts, years in business, awards, certifications, specific ZIP codes, specific neighborhood names, local ordinances, or any local detail you are not confident is true. Describe the connection itself (fast, local, responsive), not an unverified quality-control process. Always frame the work as done by the independent local providers this business connects customers to. Never claim to be factory authorized, manufacturer certified, or an approved warranty servicer. Do not quote prices, call-out fees, or parts availability. Do not promise same-day or next-day service as a guarantee — describe it as often available, never certain. Do not name a brand as serviced unless it appears in the site's own brand pages. Never state how long a repair will take or how long a part will last.
Tone: practical and reassuring — a dead fridge is urgent, but the repair itself is routine work. Write in original wording; do not copy competitor phrasing.
